kept.excerpt: The assessment form contains six criteria by which the teams' fair play performance shall be judged, stressing the positive aspects rather than negative. Red and yellow cards shall be deducted from a maximum of 10 points: first yellow card minus 1 point; second yellow/indirect red card minus 3 points; direct red card minus 4 points; yellow card and direct red card minus 5 points. Every match in the final competition shall be taken into account. FIFA shall compile and publish the classification at the end of the final competition; its decision is final.
kept.publisher: FIFA, regulations reproduced by Jus Mundi
kept.relevance: Annexe B establishes that the award depends on FIFA's assessment across several criteria and all tournament matches, so card totals alone cannot determine Norway's chances.

kept.excerpt: Brazil have won four World Cup Fair Play Awards, while England and Spain have won three each. England and France shared the award in 1998, and Brazil and Spain shared it in 2006. The listed winners from 1970 through 2022 do not include Norway.
kept.relevance: FIFA's historical list provides the award's base-rate context and confirms that multiple national winners have previously been announced.

kept.excerpt: England have not left World Cup 2022 empty-handed after picking up the Fair Play Award. The Three Lions crashed out at the quarter-final stage to eventual runners-up France, but have something to show for their efforts in Qatar after being shown just one yellow card across five games.
kept.relevance: The most recent completed men's World Cup illustrates that a quarter-final exit can still produce the Fair Play Award and supplies a concrete disciplinary benchmark.

kept.excerpt: Erling Haaland struck two late goals as Norway stunned record five-times champions Brazil 2-1 in the World Cup last 16 on Sunday to send the Scandinavian team into the quarter-finals for the first time. With their fans hugely outnumbered and in conditions that felt like a sauna, Norway tuned out the noise and the heat.
kept.relevance: This near-cutoff report establishes that Norway had advanced well beyond the group stage and still had additional matches ahead that could affect its fair-play assessment.

kept.excerpt: Erling Haaland joined Kylian Mbappé and Lionel Messi on seven goals at the 2026 FIFA World Cup as he helped Norway beat Brazil 2-1 in their last 16 clash. A date against England or Mexico awaits in the last eight on 11 July. Neymar eventually found a way past Nyland in the 100th minute from the spot after Leo Østigård was penalised for an elbow on Casemiro.
kept.relevance: This dated statistical report identifies Norway's next scheduled assessment exposure and a specific adverse conduct incident without assuming that it resulted in a disciplinary card.

kept.excerpt: Norway have announced their 26-man squad for the FIFA World Cup 2026. Stale Solbakken's squad are returning to the global finals for the first time since France 1998 and boast a bevy of big European stars that will take on France, Iraq and Senegal in Group I.
kept.relevance: This official pre-tournament source establishes Norway's participation, coach and group, while documenting the long gap since its previous World Cup appearance.
